want.who_she_is: June, 24. Left for a city job and a man, lost both, came back on a coach with two bags. Her room is half a storage room; the house has one bathroom; her bedroom door has no lock.
want.appetite: To be wanted — not looked after, not tolerated, not managed — by the people who have only ever seen her as the kid. It cannot complete: each person can go further, each room can turn.
want.ascent: Bottom: she knocks, waits for the bathroom, wears the robe over the towel, is careful in rooms that were never hers. Top: nobody knocks, the bathroom door stays open, the garage and the box room and her father's room are simply places she goes — and nobody in the house says the word for what has happened.
want.charge_note: She was the one who got out. Now she is broke in her father's house and the men who were beneath her in that story have what she needs. The taboo is the second layer; the first is that they get to watch her come down.

why_this_person.npc_ray: He was the proud one, and his approval is what she came back without. He is careful, so every inch is expensive and deniable — which makes an inch feel like a mile.
why_this_person.npc_dean: He was the disappointment while she was the success. Now they are level and he is enjoying it out loud. Wanting him is wanting the person who is winning.
why_this_person.npc_cal: Nineteen, obvious, transparently gone on her. The easy rung — she finds out what she is willing to do on someone who will never say no, which is its own kind of ugly.
why_this_person.npc_marek: A stranger inside the house who owes her nothing and is owed nothing, and who leaves. The rotating slot.

want.register_rule: The crude register lives on the STANDING surfaces — the bathroom, the kitchen at night, the front room after eleven, her own room with the door not shut. One-time scenes may be careful; the content she returns to fifty times is the crude content.

Two interactive family members CANNOT share a scene. Every scene is her plus exactly one of them; a second body may be narrated in and flag-gated.

locations.job: The house collects here after dark — whoever is home ends up in it, and after eleven it is usually only one of them.
The crossing point. Everyone passes through, nobody stays — so it is where she is caught in passing.
The private male space. Nothing in it is hers, and both of them know when she comes out.
The vantage. Boards give her away; from here she can hear the water and see the light under the bathroom door. Corridor — legitimately thin.
Her base, and half storage. The door catch is broken, so it is the room privacy is supposed to happen in and does not.
The occupancy engine. One bathroom, four adults — contention, waiting, walking in, being walked in on.
The renewable slot. A stranger living on the other side of her wall, replaced every few releases.
Money that is hers, and the world that does not know. The release valve.

characters.why_wanted: the proud one, watching her come down, then wanting her anyway
the one who is winning now
the easy rung she practises on
owes nothing, is owed nothing, leaves

decisions.note: The house is ROOMS, not one location. Presence and occupancy are per-location in this engine, so room-level co-location — the whole engine of a household game — only works if rooms are locations. Cost: eight locations to fill instead of three.

the_landing exists to be the VANTAGE the bathroom is peeped from (npc_at_location, generators/v2.py:3480 and :4131-4146). It is a corridor and is expected to stay thin; the reference game's seed had a 302-word bus station.

Anchor is the_front_room, not the_bathroom. The bathroom generates the most CHARGED beats but they are short; the front room hosts the evening routine with all three men rotating through it, so it carries the most standing prose. Gate 1 also requires the anchor be reachable and re-enterable — the measured failure case had a 29% anchor inside a sealed room.
Marek works nights, so he is home alone with her while the house is empty. That is deliberate: it gives the rotating slot a window no family member competes for.

Family labelled as step- throughout. The fiction reads as family; the labels keep every distribution venue open. One venue's tag index carries /tag/stepmom/ while /tag/incest/ 404s, a platform tightened its terms in March 2026 and soft-banned a same-engine flagship, and the top-ranked game in our own corpus uses stepmom 685 times. OPEN RISK: Patreon's own terms are not captured in our research, and Patreon is the money.

BUILD ORDER FLIPPED, and this should become doctrine. Gate 2 wants >=7.5% of beats explicit, but nerve/exposure/need all start at 0 — a seduction ladder at tier 0 is absurd. The reference game resolves it the same way: its early heat is not chosen by the player at all. So the explicit floor at v0.1 is carried by the TRIGGERED layer (things that happen TO her) and the STANDING ladder stays cold until she has climbed it. The bathroom was therefore built first, not third.

SOFT-LOCK found by live play, not by any gate. The opening lands at 17:18, sleep was gated 21:00+, the shift needs the shop, and navigation does NOT advance the clock — so no scheduled window in the game was reachable, ever. Fixed with activity_evening at the front room (+90 min), which also feeds the anchor's word count, plus widening sleep to 20:00. No static check would have caught this.

COLD START found by live play. Ray and Cal only used the bathroom on weekdays and the game started Friday evening, so the core mechanic was dead until Monday — three in-game days. That was mechanical scheduling rather than fiction: people wash at weekends. Added weekend bathroom rows (Ray 09:30-10:15, Cal 11:00-11:50) and moved the start to Sunday so Monday morning is day 2.

PROSE CAUGHT BY ITS OWN GATE. The first draft of the peep and walk-in scenes scored 0.0% on the explicit floor despite being explicit, because the prose named the act obliquely — 'hard', 'comes', 'finishes' — instead of naming bodies. That is exactly the defect diagnosed in the previous game. Rewriting seven beats in a crude register took the floor 0.0% -> 12.0% and flipped three gates. The wordlist was NOT loosened: 'come' would match 'come downstairs' everywhere, so excluding it is correct and the prose was the thing at fault.

TOML SYNTAX: exit blocks must use SECTION syntax ([canvases.nodes.exit_block] + [[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]), not nested inline tables. A multi-line inline table is a parse error, and a conditional choice list is unavoidably multi-line. The shipped game does this 199 times; I wrote it inline first and the merge failed. `conditions = { ... items = [ ... ] }` may span lines because newlines are legal inside the array — two levels of nesting is where it breaks.

METER CEILING caught a real lie. `nerve` displayed a 75-100 top band while the highest authored gate was 75, so the top 25 points bought nothing. Fixed by making the top band UNBOUNDED (min=75, no max) on all three tiers — which is honest (75 IS the top rung) and which the gate correctly skips as promising nothing.

GATE CORRECTED: meter ceiling. With top bands correctly unbounded, the old check read the SECOND band's max as the ceiling and produced nonsense ('exposure shown up to 74'). The truer semantic is that EVERY BAND BOUNDARY IS A PROMISE — a meter showing 15/35/55/75 tells the player something is different at each. The gate now compares the highest authored gate against the TOP band's min and names the empty bands: 'exposure: bands promise something at 35/55/75, but the highest authored gate is 15'. Vesper unchanged at 1/10.

Ray's top rung OMITS locked_text on purpose, so the greyed row shows the action ('Ask him for it in front of the others') — a want the player can name — rather than a reason they cannot act. Cal's still shows the reason; compare both before ship and pick one house style.

ENGINE RULE that HARD-FAILS the build: a flag read by a TRIGGER must be set from a canvas that HAS a location/schedule. `dean_open` was set in the exit of a triggerless rung and read by hub_dean_late's trigger; the flag-chain validator refused the build with 'MISSING HINT - set by ... but no location/schedule' — it cannot tell the player where to go to earn a flag set inside a link target. Fix: move the flagEffects onto the hub CHOICE that opens the rung. Same semantics, located canvas, chain resolves. Flags nothing reads in a trigger are unaffected.

THE MOST DANGEROUS FAILURE CLASS SO FAR: an unrecognised TOML key is SILENTLY IGNORED. I wrote `clothingEffects = [{itemId, op='grant'}]` to grant the two garments. The TOML parsed, the validator passed, the build went green — and nothing was ever granted, which would have left the top of the wardrobe permanently unreachable with no error anywhere. The real key is `wardrobeEffects = [{action='add', item_id='...'}]` on exit_block.config. Nothing in the pipeline catches an invented key; the only defence is to grep template_import.py for any key not personally seen in a shipped game.

HER ROOM built out from 68 words: the boxes (milestone -> grants the wardrobe's top tier), activity_get_dressed (banded on worn_corruption), activity_the_door (the broken catch, banded on exposure — the room's whole thesis: she has stopped meaning to fix it), and activity_alone (solo, gated arousal>=30, banded on nerve so what she thinks about changes as she climbs). THE REGISTER DEFECT IS MINE AND IT RECURS. Third time. The new peeps and walk-ins added SIXTEEN beats and ZERO explicit ones — every new beat scored 0 or 1 against the 3-word floor, dropping the game to exactly 7.5%. The pattern is always the same: name a body part once, then pivot the next beat to psychology (he knows / her face burning / what it means). The heat sits in the situation and never in the words. This is Vesper's diagnosed defect reproduced by the same author who wrote the doctrine against it, twice after writing it. THE FIX IS NOT WORD-STUFFING: stay on the body THROUGH the beat instead of referencing it once and moving on. Eleven targeted rewrites took the floor 7.5% -> 9.4%, which is at the TOP of the reference game's measured 7.5-9.3% band. Conclusion for the skill: this is not a lapse, it is a default that reasserts itself the moment it is not being actively fought, and the gate is the only thing that catches it.

THE MORNING QUEUE VERIFIED LIVE. Added Dean a bathroom row (07:40-08:00 weekdays), which he lacked entirely — he could neither be peeped nor walk in on anything. Grid now steps cleanly: 06:45 Ray, 07:20 Cal, 07:50 Dean, 08:30 empty, no overlaps. Each of the four peeps is offered only while its own man is in its own room, including Marek's box-room peep at Tuesday 11:00 which needed no new schedule row because his door was already established as half open.

PLANTED FACTS PAID. All three night-one details now have content hanging off them: the gap down the hinge side (four peeps), the extractor that makes her deaf (three walk-ins hung off activity_wash's substitutions at rising exposure), and the eighteen-inch wall (activity_the_wall, banded on nerve — at the bottom she is trying not to hear it, at the top she is timing herself to it).

THE DOCTRINE WORKS, AND THIS WAS ITS TEST. references/register.md was written first, then the kitchen was authored against it. Result: beats 106 -> 120 (+14) and the explicit floor 9.4% -> 10.0% — the floor went UP. For four consecutive increments before this, new content dropped it and had to be rewritten after the gate caught it. The rule that did it: an explicit beat stays on the body for its whole length, and the interiority gets its OWN beat afterwards rather than being folded into the act. Splitting them costs nothing (cascade beats are free) and sacrifices none of the psychology.

THE MISSING DOCTRINE FILE. The skill said WHERE the crude register lives and WHICH words were permitted, and nothing about HOW to write the beat — which is why the same author reproduced the defect three times after writing the doctrine against it. references/register.md now names the three pivot targets explicitly (he knows / she is ashamed / what this says about her) so they are catchable while writing, and states that the fix is duration on the body, NOT word-stuffing and NOT loosening the frozen wordlist.

KITCHEN built out 698 -> 1,775. Four surfaces against the existing schedule: Cal 07:40-08:00 (twenty minutes, cannot look at her, and the cupboard is above his head), Dean 08:00-09:00 (down from the bathroom she watched him in — the whole scene is the not-mentioning), Marek 16:00-17:30 (the only hour the two of them are the only adults in the house, and the only meal anyone eats sitting down). Marek and Cal both now carry two surfaces.

THE ANCHOR TRAP — a ratio gate tightens as you work elsewhere. Gate 1 wants the anchor at >=25% of ALL location prose, so the front room's share fell 53% -> 46% -> 40% -> 39% -> 35% while six other rooms were written and not one word was removed from it. Held at 4,020 it would have crossed below 25% within a single further increment, taking the game 9/10 -> 8/10 while getting objectively better. Budget the anchor against the FINISHED total: at 36,000 it owes 9,000. Recorded in references/the-board.md as 'fill the anchor IN STEP with the rest'.

FLAG-CHAIN RULE IS BROADER THAN RECORDED. Hit it a second time with ray_arrangement: the validator refuses a flag set in a triggerless rung when it is read by a CHOICE condition, not only by a trigger. Same fix both times — move the flagEffects up onto the located hub choice that opens the rung. engine.md §16 corrected to say 'a TRIGGER or a CHOICE'.

THE LAST EMPTY SCHEDULE ROW IS FILLED. Dean was present in the garage 14:00-17:00 at weekends with zero content — the only scheduled row in the game with nothing on it. Verified live at Saturday 15:00: getNpcsAtLocation('the_garage') returns ['npc_dean'] and his hub renders. He now carries three surfaces (kitchen, front room late, garage).

SCOPE HONESTY: the plan named three targets and this increment hit two. Garage 309 -> ~1,600 and the front room 4,020 -> ~5,000 (the anchor instalment, verified live at Monday 01:00). THE BOX ROOM WAS NOT TOUCHED and remains at 908 — it carries into the next increment rather than being quietly dropped.

AUTHORING BUG CAUGHT IN MY OWN PROSE: Hannah Beckett's line in canvas_someone_who_knew was written as a `dialog` block attributed to npcId=npc_marek, because she is a walk-on with no NPC record. It would have rendered 'Marek:' over a woman's line in the built game. Fixed by making it quoted prose in a paragraph. THE STRUCTURAL REASON WALK-ONS MUST BE PROSE: adding Hannah as an [[npcs]] entry would immediately BREAK gate 6, which requires every declared character to have a standing surface and a schedule row. The gate is right — a character with a name and no way to find them is the defect it exists to catch — so one-scene characters are narrated, never declared.

A USEFUL LINT, worth adding to gates.py later: flag any `dialog` block whose npcId is a character the canvas neither BINDS (npc/requires_npc) nor NAMES in its id. Run over back_home it returns exactly 2 hits, both canvas_arrival (which legitimately has Ray and Dean speaking in the opening), and it WOULD have caught the Hannah bug. The naive version — flagging dialogue on any unbound canvas — returns 30 false positives, because every triggerless rung is unbound by design and correctly carries its own character's voice.

THE SHOP IS THE MIRROR. Built 76 -> ~1,000: the regulars banded on `pride` (the same six hours read as humiliation, then as rest, then as camouflage), and canvas_someone_who_knew — a woman she sat next to for two years, who does the face badly. The point of the shop is that it is the ONLY place the reversal is visible from outside the house, and from out there the story is short and finished: June went, June came back, June is at the shop. The house is the only part still moving.
